chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Yaʿqūb ibn Yazīd, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from some of our companions, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said:
The kurr of water, which nothing renders impure, is one thousand and two hundred ritls.

So this report does not conflict with the reports that preceded it, because we had mentioned in our book Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām that acting upon this report is according to what the Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, supported. And we interpreted what was reported concerning specification by spans as being in conformity with that, such that their measure would be the measure that corresponds to it. Thus it is as though two methods were established for us: one of them is that we consider ritls when we have a way to determine them, and if there is no way to that, we consider spans, because that is not impossible in any circumstance. The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, chose regarding the ritls that they be according to the Baghdadi measure, while others among our companions held that they be according to the Madani measure. There is no report here that includes mention of ritls other than this report, and despite that it is also mursal, even if it is repeated in the books, for its basis is Ibn Abī ʿUmayr from some of our companions. The view that the Baghdadi ritls are to be considered is closer to correctness, because they approximate the measure that we adopted in spans; but if we consider the Madani measure, the approximation between them becomes remote. So acting upon that is more appropriate for what we have already stated, and what further strengthens this consideration is also what...

key_terms.الْأَشْبَارِ: handspans used as an alternative method of measurement
key_terms.الْبَغْدَادِيَّةِ: the Baghdadi standard of ritl measurement
key_terms.الْكُرُّ: the legal threshold quantity of water that is not easily rendered impure
key_terms.الْمَاءِ: water, the subject of the purity ruling
key_terms.الْمَدَنِيِّ: the Madani standard of ritl measurement
key_terms.رِطْلٍ: a unit of weight/measure used here to quantify kurr
key_terms.مُرْسَلٌ: a report with a missing link in its sanad

ai.seo_question: How does al-Istibṣār reconcile the hadiths that measure kurr water by ritls and by spans?
ai.summary: This passage discusses the legal measure of kurr water, the quantity of water that is not rendered impure by mere contact with impurity. It reconciles the report measuring kurr by ritls with other reports measuring it by spans, and prefers the Baghdadi ritl because it aligns more closely with the span-based calculation.
